newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says new budget another step to balance.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says new budget another step to balance.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Saturday hailed a budget compromise between the White House and Congress as more progress toward a balanced budget and praised Republicans for working in a bipartisan fashion.
"It is good for America because it continues to move us toward a balanced budget while protecting, not violating, our values," Clinton told a campaign rally in Providence.

Clinton, appearing at the rally with retiring Rhode Island Democrat Sen. Claiborne Pell, said the budget includes the biggest increase in Pell Grant college scholarships in 20 years. He said it will put 40,000 more young children in Head Start programs, continue his program to connect classrooms to the Internet, and fund clean air, water and safe food.

Clinton said the budget deal reflected an "abandonment" of Republican attempts to lift the ban on 17 types of assault weapons and expands the Brady Bill handgun control bill to deny guns to those who commit domestic abuse against a spouse.

"In the last three months as the American people have made it clear that they have no intention of seeing our country torn apart and divided over a radical agenda, we have restored a measure of bipartisanship and working together in Washington. Look what happens when you abandon extremism in favor of working together," he said.
